title: Making an Impact That Lasts: Mitchell Stewart Awarded as Veteran of the Year
summary: We highly value service at Sonoco. Practicing this value can look slightly different in an office than on a production floor, but the heart of placing others’ needs before our own remains the same.
body_markdown:
We highly value service at Sonoco. Practicing this value can look slightly different in an office than on a production floor, but the heart of placing others’ needs before our own remains the same. For some team members, service is more than a workplace value. It’s a mindset they learned and put into practice long before working at Sonoco, like Mitchell Stewart, a Navy Veteran and Team Leader at the Sonoco Recycling facility in Charlotte, North Carolina.


In recognition of his consistent dedication, leadership and integrity in his workplace, the Military Professionals Employee Resource Group (ERG) at Sonoco awarded Stewart with the 2026 Veteran of the Year award. We asked him to share how his service shaped his approach to work, what this award means to him, what advice he’d offer other veterans and more.


### How did your time in the military prepare you for work at Sonoco?


My time in the military taught me to take more initiative. When I first started at Sonoco, I quickly learned to be proactive about fixing issues. Rather than sitting back and relying on others to deal with problems, I’d watch my manager fix machinery issues so that I could fix it myself the next time. Even though my first role was mostly janitorial, my military service equipped me with the skills to focus on a solution, work under pressure and not get bogged down by the problem.


### What does service mean to you today?


Outside of work, I’m a minister in the church, so I’m always trying to help somebody out any way that I can wherever I am. Sometimes that looks like listening to a team member share details about their bad day or, like happened the other day, jump-starting someone’s car battery in the parking lot of my local grocery store. I may not always be able to completely solve the problem, but I can help.


### What led to your career at Sonoco?


After serving in the Navy for four years, I wanted to see my kids take their first steps, go to school and achieve other milestones. When I came home and started my job search, my father worked at Sonoco and brought me on. I started with sweeping floors, cleaning up and operating manual equipment, and then I kept progressing and learning different things, like Safety.


Before being acquired by Sonoco, my facility did not make safety as high of a priority. At first, no one wanted to share the need for more Safety structure, so I volunteered to do it. Now Safety is a high priority and a key part of each day. I like the fact that we have clear rules. Everything has a place and a process, and I get to be part of that.


### What advice would you offer to veterans interested in a manufacturing career?


The military and manufacturing have a lot in common. Everyone has a job to do. In manufacturing, everyone needs to do a job until they can complete a JSA (Job Safety Analysis) and know how to do the job. In the military, it’s similar. When maintenance is needed, everyone has a maintenance call to pull and follow step-by-step. Both environments have clear structure.


### What do enjoy about your Team Leader role?


I like my relationships with my coworkers. When I started as a Safety Coordinator and later moved into a leadership role, I had to learn how to talk to people better, because I had to explain why we do what we do.


In the military, leaders can sometimes expect that once they tell people to go do something, they’ll just do it. Outside of the military, people typically don’t respond well to that approach. They need more, a real relationship or an explanation. I learned this skill through leading and training, so I can better communicate and connect with people at and outside of work without assuming anything.


### What accomplishment are you most proud of in your time at Sonoco?


Before working at Sonoco, I didn’t even know how to drive a tractor and trailer. During my 35 years at Sonoco, I not only learned how to drive a truck and trailer, a forklift, front-end loader and more, but I also learned how to work on bailers.


Thanks to having good managers throughout my time at Sonoco, I’ve learned many new skills that I can use outside of work. Earlier in my career, one manager took me under his wing and helped me develop the confidence to figure things out and even fix things in my home without renting supplies or calling somebody.


### What does winning the Veteran of the Year award mean to you?


Winning was very unexpected, but I’m very proud to receive this honor. It just shows that somebody sees you and the work you do, and I really appreciate that recognition.
